title: Cross-seed minimal layer-coalition transfer
objective: Discover a minimum-cardinality answer-position attention-write layer mask in one frozen model per depth, then test the identical mask on two unseen seeds at the same depth.
primary_claim: A discovery-selected layer coalition transfers the h01/h11 contrast bidirectionally and by donor identity on all held-out same-depth models.
secondary_claims: The transported coalition remains inclusion-minimal on held-out models.
The coalition is sparse, with cardinality no greater than half the network depth.
Matched MLP writes do not automatically reproduce the selected attention coalition.

design.candidate_masks: all 2^L masks including the empty and full controls
design.selection: minimum cardinality, then lexicographic layer tuple, among simultaneous-confidence-certified masks
design.confirmation: same frozen mask on the exhaustive finite task population and held-out seeds

interventions: correct h11 attention writes into h01
reverse h01 attention writes into h11
claim_boundaries: A contrast-switching coalition is not a proof that its members are individually necessary under natural execution.
Teacher-forced component writes contain oracle trajectory information.
Layer indices are compared only within the same architecture depth.
No head, neuron, pretrained model, natural-language, or cross-architecture claim is authorized by registration alone.
hard_stops: No threshold, seed, mask, donor, or component may change after preregistration.
Held-out seeds and exhaustive confirmation results cannot select the mask.
Failure closes synthetic layer-coalition localization instead of starting another mask search.
Head-level analysis requires the primary, shared-minimality, and sparsity gates together.
